name: Human Gut Cell Atlas (HGCA) v1 - All Cells
description: Healthy and adjacent-to-disease control data from 27 gut single-cell RNAseq datasets were collected and integrated to form v1 of the Human Gut Cell Atlas

labelsets.name: hgca_celltype_v0
labelsets.description: Cell annotations (Prelim annotation) are based on the finest possible label that could be used to describe each of the ~500 clusters found during integration and subclustering

labels.name: Cycling TA
labels.fullName: Transiently amplifying cells with predominant cycling signature
labels.rationale: TA with ONLY cell cycle markers
labels.ontologyAssessment: This may be redundant with the overall TA label. Maybe we should collapse these

labels.name: Absorptive TA
labels.fullName: Transiently amplifying cells with predominant absorptive signature
labels.rationale: NOTCH1 and low expression of absorptive markers such as FABP or ALDOB show an early bias towards absorptive lineage
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Colonocytes Early
labels.rationale: Residual developmental signaling, LEFTY1, and newly upregulated colon microenvironment related genes point to an earlier colonocyte subtype
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Secretory Goblet Cells
labels.rationale: Intestinal goblet cells which produce mucus. These are easily found in scRNA data with MUC2, TFF3, and REG4

labels.name: Colonocytes Laminin
labels.rationale: We found a common subcluster of hypothetically basement membrane laminin producing specialized colonocytes which we separate as an outgroup here based on multiple basement membrane scaffold proteins, LAMA and MUC17
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Colonocytes Late
labels.rationale: mature/late colonocytes are defined here by ion regulation genes (SLC, AQP) and cell adhesion markers (CEACAM)
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Secretory TA
labels.fullName: Transiently amplifying cells with predominant secretory signature
labels.rationale: TA biased towards secretory fate, we also define these with distinct differentiation markers HEPACAM2 and ANXA13
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Follicle associated enterocyte (FAE)
labels.rationale: a high abundance of CCL genes and IL15 in absorptive epithelial subclusters points to a potentially follicle associated enterocyte group. CCL20 is the canonical marker for these, but isn't found in marker lists.

labels.name: junk
labels.rationale: A Cell Annotation Platform (CAP) term used to identify a row in a “cell by gene” table that appears to contain non-cellular data rather than data from one cell and should therefore be discarded.

labels.name: Secretory Goblet cells Mature
labels.rationale: Intestinal goblet cells with high TFF1 expression, indicating terminal differentiation / maturity

labels.name: Enterocytes Early
labels.rationale: Enterocytes which have developed into absorptive lineage from TA and progenitor subtypes first express ANPEP, ALDOB, and other enzymes
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: Secretory Tuft Cells
labels.rationale: Tuft cells are rare in single cell data, these often have POU2F3 in gene lists but LRMP is a more distinct marker

labels.name: Microfold Cells (M Cells)
labels.rationale: Antigen sampling cells that transport lumen antigens to the immune compartment below them. These can be difficult to identify because canonical markers like SPIB are found in enterocytes as well. Some subclusters were high in NOS2 and TGM2 so we gave this label

labels.name: Transiently Amplifying Cells (TA)
labels.rationale: TA are defined as rapidly cycling epithelial progenitors that sit between stem cells and differentiated absorptive, secretory, or defensive cells. Usually defined by a strong cycling signature, we split these into absorptive/secretory/cycling subtypes with weaker lineage specific signatures than their descendants

labels.name: Epithelial Stem Cells (LGR5+)
labels.rationale: LGR5 expression is a clear determinant of epith stem cells

labels.name: Enterocytes
labels.rationale: Enterocytes here are the absorptive epithelial cells of the small intestine. These express high levels of keratin and mitochondrial genes and are unique in each suborgan - duodenum and ileum. We should think about how to categorize duodenal vs. jejunal vs ileal enterocytes. EPCAM is the lineage defining marker here but does not appear in single cell data. Here, enterocytes are subdivided into early and late lifecycle subtypes, when neither of these can be determined, the broader label is used

labels.name: Colonocytes
labels.rationale: Colonocytes are the absorptive epithelial cells of the large intestine. Similar to enterocytes, these are subdivided into early and late stage, and when neither of these can be determined, this broader description is used. Hypoxia-related markers are used to differentiate colonocytes from other absorptive epithelial cells due to the less regulated tissue microenvironment.

labels.name: Colonocytes BEST4
labels.rationale: BEST4 is found to differentiate a subcluster of colonocytes across multiple gut epithelial datasets, and is often the only marker needed to identify this subset

labels.name: EEC L Cells (PYY+)
labels.rationale: PYY alone is enough to identify

labels.name: EEC Enterochromaffin Cells
labels.rationale: EEC which produce primarily TPH1 and CHGA. TPH1 differentiates from broader EEC label

labels.name: Enteroendocrine Cells (EEC)
labels.rationale: This is the broader term for EEC when a subtype could not be identified. These are identified by CHGA and CHGB, and their canonical differentiation marker NEUROD1.

labels.name: EEC Progenitor
labels.rationale: NEUROG3 expression identifies EEC subclusters that are just starting their differentiation away from secretory progenitor / epithstem identity towards EEC subtypes

labels.name: Enterocytes Late
labels.rationale: Enterocytes which are maturing closer to the lumen upregulate lipid packaging (APO) and DUOX2, an antimicrobial oxidase most active in the apical cells of the villi.
labels.ontologyAssessment: Since absorptive epithelial cells lay on a continuum, it's not clear if or how we should have subdivisions of epithelial subtypes. We argue it could be useful for high-res compositional analysis to have some type of subdivision.

labels.name: EEC N Cells
labels.rationale: NTS alone is enough to identify

labels.name: Enterocytes BEST4
labels.rationale: A BEST4 enterocyte population is annotated for some clusters enriched in SI. These tend to have other antimicrobial/mucus regulating/ionic gradient enzymes upregulated as well

labels.name: Secretory Paneth Cells
labels.rationale: Paneth cells are found mostly in small intestine and are identified here with defensins DEFA* alongside high PLA2G2A. These are even rarer than tuft cells

labels.name: doublets
labels.rationale: A Cell Annotation Platform (CAP) term used to identify a row in a “cell by gene” table that appears to contain combined data from a pair of cells rather than data from one cell and should therefore be discarded.

labels.name: EEC S Cells (SCT+)
labels.rationale: SCT alone is enough to identify

labels.name: Monocytes
labels.rationale: Cells of other lineages are sometimes sorted by the border of broad clusters. These appear to be monocytes of myeloid lineage

labels.name: CD4 Th17
labels.rationale: Since both ILC3s and Th17 express RORC and IL7R, these can be difficult to separate. Th17 were annotated when larger clusters of naive T cells showed a clear IL7R and RORC expressing subcluster

labels.name: CD8 Effector/Memory
labels.fullName: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell, terminally differentiated
labels.ontologyTerm: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell, terminally differentiated
labels.rationale: No CX3CR1 but IL2, granzymes, and CD8 signatures are found abundantly in single cell data of the gut

labels.name: T NKT
labels.rationale: ZBTB16 expressing, CD7, JUND, NKG7, these could be NK T cells - but not sure of TCR expression
labels.ontologyAssessment: unconventional T cell category would be useful to encapsulate non-CD8/CD4 t cell subclasses. https://doi.org/10.1038/ni.3298

labels.name: CD8 Circulating Effector/Memory
labels.fullName: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
labels.ontologyTerm: effector memory CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
labels.rationale: KLRG1, FGFBP2, CX3CR1, GZMH expressing set of clusters found across tissue sections

labels.name: CD8 TRM
labels.rationale: ITGAE and RORA point to granzyme positive t resident memory populations, and clusters of these tend to be more unique to certain sections of the gut, driving down the number of datasets they are found in (dataset diversity metric)
synonyms: tissue resident memory CD8 T cell

labels.name: CD4 Naive
labels.rationale: CD4 Naive T cells are defined as CCR7, IL7R, LEF1 and SELL expressing signatures

labels.name: CD8 IEL
labels.rationale: A large cluster of ITGAE high, CD160 exists in the atlas, pointing to resident status. contextualization with radial tissue terms could increase evidence

labels.name: T Cycling
labels.rationale: Cycling T cells were annotated based on STMN1, MKI67 and other cell cycle genes alongside a T lineage background, including TRAC

labels.name: B Atypical
labels.rationale: FCRL4 and FCRL5 point to atypical B cells, but ITGAX was not found here
labels.ontologyAssessment: atypical/unconventional B and T cell groups could be useful for hierarchical consistency?

labels.name: CD4 Memory
labels.rationale: When CD4 celltypes show no clear evidence of Treg, Naive, or Th states, but contain a clear interleukin, MAF, and differentiated signal, we annotate them as CD4 Memory

labels.name: B Marginal zone (MZB)
labels.fullName: marginal zone B cell of lymph node
labels.ontologyTerm: marginal zone B cell of lymph node
labels.rationale: FCRL1, CD1C with HLA, CD79 signatures point to potential MZB cells

labels.name: ILC NK Cells
labels.rationale: Marker lists with high NKG7 and GNLY point to NK subsets

labels.name: Plasma IGA
labels.rationale: These are easily distinguished from other plasma subsets via IGHA variants

labels.name: CD4 Treg
labels.rationale: Coexpress FOXP3 and IL2RA (CD25), FOXP3 expression quickly identifies clusters of T-regs

labels.name: CD4 Th1
labels.rationale: Th1 are annotated when CD4 cells show IFNG or TNF program signatures and especially IL7R. Thelper cytotoxic dual signatures point then to Th1

labels.name: CD4 Tfh
labels.rationale: CD40LG and ICOS are used to annotate Tfh in this data. These are also found in larger clusters of CD4 naive cells

labels.name: GC B Light Zone
labels.rationale: BANK1 is found in all subsets annotated as LZ, TNFRSF13C supports in some

labels.name: ILC3
labels.rationale: KRT86, RORC, IL7R and IL23R point to strong ILC3 signature, while some nearby subclusters show a more ILC or ILC2 tilt

labels.name: B Memory
labels.rationale: CD27, HLA-DRA, SELL, and CD69 separated memory B cells from other B subsets

labels.name: ILC2
labels.rationale: ST2 is found in one subcluster of ~1000 cells among other ILC clusters, pointing to ILC2. 16_0 could also be ILC2 due to ST2 expression

labels.name: CD8 T
labels.rationale: broadly annotated when CD8 T cells didn't show sufficient markers to resolve finer states

labels.name: GC B Dark Zone
labels.rationale: CXCR4 high with CD83 point to Dark zone

labels.name: B Naive
labels.rationale: MARCKSL1 and IGHD were found in some subclusters found near other follicular B cells. These have high HLA genes, CD79A and B

labels.name: CD8 Memory/Exhausted
labels.rationale: TOX, CD27, GZM pointed to CD8 memory here, and HAVCR2 pointed to an exhausted signature

labels.name: CD8 Naive
labels.fullName: naive thymus-derived CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
labels.ontologyTerm: naive thymus-derived CD8-positive, alpha-beta T cell
labels.rationale: Proximity to other CD8 clusters and LEF1 expression allowed me to annotate this ~7k cell sub-cluster found amongst other CD4 clusters as CD8 naive.

labels.name: T GammaDelta
labels.rationale: TRDC, TRGC2 and SOX4 point to gamma delta T cells, but these do not show the canonical TRGC9, TRDC2 variants.
labels.ontologyAssessment: unconventional T cell category would be useful to encapsulate non-CD8/CD4 t cell subclasses. https://doi.org/10.1038/ni.3298

labels.name: B Cycling
labels.rationale: B cells (HLA, CD79) with clear STMN1 and other cell cycle signal

labels.name: Plasma Cells
labels.rationale: Cells of other lineages are sometimes sorted by the border of broad clusters. These appear to be plasma cells of lymphoid lineage

labels.name: Plasma IGG
labels.rationale: IGHG

labels.name: ILC1
labels.rationale: General ILC signature with IFNG expression

labels.name: T MAIT
labels.rationale: This small subcluster uniquely clearly expressed the TRAV1-2 MAIT TCR marker

labels.name: Macrophages Cycling
labels.rationale: Coexpression of MKI67, STMN1, and often histones with macrophage core genes (C1QB, MS4A7) identify proliferating macrophages engaged in local self renewal or inflammatory expansion

labels.name: Macrophages Tissue Resident
labels.rationale: High C1QA, C1QB, C1QC, SELENOP and phagocytic/lysosomal programs point to the long lived tissue resident macrophages that are distinct from monocyte derived circulating lineages

labels.name: DC cDC2
labels.rationale: CD1C, CLEC10A, FCER1A, SIRPA, define antigen presenting type 2 conventional dendritic cells with CD11b positive identity and non crosspresenting functions

labels.name: DC cDC1
labels.rationale: Expresses CLEC9A, XCR1, DNASE1L3, and related cross presentation machinery, matching the canonical transcriptional program of type 1 conventional dendritic cells described in human mucosal and lymphoid tissues

labels.name: DC migDC
labels.rationale: LAMP3, CCR7, IDO1, CD40, CCL5, capture the antigen experienced, lymph node directed migratory DC state which has been repeatedly observed in barrier tissues
labels.ontologyAssessment: migratory DCs are a well described rare celltype relevant to mucosal biology that are increasingly being annotated in single cell atlases - they should have a cell ontology label!

labels.name: Fibroblasts Follicular Dendritic Cells (fDC)
labels.rationale: Displays CR1, CR2, CXCL13, TNFSF13B, and complement receptor driven antigen retention machinery. These also express stroma lineage markers, making them easy to annotate within the myeloid lineage.

labels.name: Macrophages M2
labels.rationale: Expresses MRC1 (CD206), FOLR2, CD163L1, CD209, and other alternative activation metabolic genes, marking tissue repair and IL4/IL13 responsive programs

labels.name: Granulocytes Mast Cells
labels.rationale: presence of KIT, FCER1A, FCER1G could point to matured Mast cells with chymase, something to look out for here. In general, CPA3 and tryptase (TPSAB*) genes are highly expressed and unique to mast cell populations, making them easy to annotate in gut data

labels.name:
DC Monocyte derived dendritic cell
(MO DC)
labels.rationale: Shows MSR1, NPR2, and monocyte-to-DC transition markers, defining monocyte-derived dendritic cells arising under inflammatory differentiation

labels.name: Granulocytes
labels.rationale: Expresses granulocytic effectors including CLC, IL4 inducible modules, CPA3, and Fcγ receptor associated genes, hint at polymorphonuclear granulocytes distinct from mast cells. Obviously a big ? given difficulty in picking these up with typical droplet-based protocols

labels.name: Epithelial
labels.rationale: These are epithelial cells that snuck into the stromal lineage object. This annotation contains cells expressing EPCAM, ANPEP, mucins, treffoils, making them difficult to classify further

labels.name: Smooth Muscle Cells (SMC)
labels.rationale: Expresses DES, TAGLN, MYH11, ACTG2 consistent with visceral smooth muscle layers of gut wall (muscularis propria/longitudinal and circular layers).

labels.name: Fibroblasts Lamina propria (S1)
labels.rationale: This label represents superficial lamina propria fibroblasts that are ADAMDEC1+, ABCA8+, FABP4+ and form the dominant fibroblast population across datasets and samples. FOS+ Fibroblast Lamina propria or Ribo(high) Fibroblast Lamina propria, and note an upper-lamina WNT4+ subset (Stroma_0_2) described in the literature, as well as plasma (IGHA+) and myeloid (C1S/C1R+) doublet-contaminated clusters. Taken together, the transcriptional program, high dataset and sample diversity, and literature on WNT4+ villus-oriented fibroblasts support a high-confidence lamina propria fibroblast identity, with FOS and ribosomal signatures reflecting activation state rather than separate cell types.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Venular
labels.rationale: Annotated by ACKR1 predominantly, these separate clearly from other vascular endothelial clusters

labels.name: Fibroblasts Crypt Bottom (S2A)
labels.rationale: S2A fibroblasts sit near the crypt base and are enriched for VSTM2A together with PDGFRA, BMP4, WNT5A, POSTN and other S2 markers. Several clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Bottom (S2A) show very low dataset diversity but reproducible expression of POSTN, F3 and BMPs, and differences between individual S2A annotation clusters are subtle (see annotation_cluster) and may largely reflect activation and quality flags (for example high mitochondrial content) rather than true subtypes. We therefore annotate a single S2A cell type corresponding to crypt-bottom fibroblasts with high-confidence positional identity and variable activation signatures.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Crypt Top (S2B)
labels.rationale: S2B fibroblasts are positioned toward the crypt top or villus tip and are characterized by NRG1 and NPY, we also highlight VEGFD and TRPA1 as convincing markers of villus-tip subepithelial fibroblasts. Clusters annotated as Fibroblasts Crypt Top (S2B) (for example Stroma_1_1 and 12_1–12_4) show these markers along with the broader S2 program and are present in multiple datasets, albeit with varying mitochondrial content and dataset diversity. We therefore treat S2B as a robust positional subtype of S2, capturing villus-tip fibroblasts with strong NRG1/VEGFD/TRPA1 signatures.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Arteriolar
labels.rationale: Arteriolar endothelial cells express SEMA3G, PLVAP, TM4SF1, MGP

labels.name: vascular endothelial Pre venule capillary (PVC)
labels.rationale: Identified by LITAF and ICAM1 expression, consistent with pre venous capillary beds positioned before venules in intestinal microcirculation.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Submucosal (aka Crypt Support/Trophocytes/S3)
labels.rationale: Submucosal S3 fibroblasts occupy deeper layers and crypt base regions and are enriched for GREM1, C7, OLFM4, PTGS2, THY1, SEMA3A and GLI1, consistent with crypt-support or trophocyte roles. Cluster-level annotations describe RSPO3, GREM1, DCN and C3 as strong markers of submucosal fibroblasts (for example Stroma_2_0) and we note that S3 populations have lower dataset diversity and appear deeper than lamina propria fibroblasts, especially in resection-derived data. Multiple clusters labeled as Fibroblasts Submucosal (aka Crypt Support/Trophocytes/S3) recur with similar signatures, supporting a distinct S3 fibroblast class even though a dedicated CL term is still needed.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Subepithelial (S2)
labels.rationale: S2 fibroblasts form a subepithelial band under the epithelium and are characterized by PDGFRA, BMP4, F3, NPY, CD34, TRPA1, SOX6, WNT5A and POSTN expression. Multiple clusters are noted as FOS+ Fibroblast Subepithelial with clear POSTN, F3 and BMP signatures and we note that TRPA1 and VEGFD are good markers higher in the villus axis, while VSTM2A and NRG1 mark bottom and top crypt positions respectively. These clusters are present across many datasets with varying activation and mitochondrial signatures, suggesting a continuum of S2 fibroblast states rather than distinct cell types.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Post arteriole capillary (PAC)
labels.rationale: RGCC and FCN3, distinguishing it from pre venule capillaries and venules in gut vasculature.

labels.name: Glia Myenteric Plexus / Type I
labels.rationale: Myenteric plexus type I glia are identified by TF, BCAN and CACLB expression on top of a pan-glial program, and occupy clusters that align with deeper muscularis propria / submucosal regions in the integrated object. These clusters are present across datasets with full-thickness or muscularis-enriched sampling, consistent with myenteric plexus localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: Glia Submucosal Plexus / Type I
labels.rationale: This label is used for type I glia associated with the submucosal plexus, distinguished by expression of ENTPD2, SFRP5 and a core glial program and by their co-clustering with other submucosal plexus markers in integrated data. They are present across several datasets but enriched in samples with preserved submucosa, consistent with a submucosal plexus localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: Pericytes Secretory
labels.rationale: MUSTN1 and PLN were used to annotate pericytes with secretory program, two putative paracrine factors

labels.name: Fibroblasts Muscularis Propria
labels.rationale: These fibroblasts are defined by DPT, C7, KCNN3, CA8 and PLCB4 expression and were initially annotated as Muscularis Propria fibroblasts in the hierarchy, but our experts repeatedly note that some clusters with this label are present in many biopsy-derived datasets, which is difficult to reconcile with a strictly muscularis-only population. Marker profiles suggest a deeper S3-like or muscle-adjacent fibroblast population, but current spatial evidence is insufficient to cleanly separate muscularis propria fibroblasts from subserosal or submucosal fibroblasts in the integrated data. We therefore keep this label as a provisional deeper muscle-layer fibroblast class with moderate confidence and flag the spatial assignment as uncertain. Do we need a "deep S3" sub-label?
labels.ontologyAssessment: Do we need a "deep S3 fibroblast" sublabel?

labels.name: Glia Mucosal/Type III
labels.rationale: Mucosal type III glia are defined by RELN, MBP and PLLP expression together with canonical glial markers, and are the predominant glial population in mucosa/submucosa-enriched samples. Several clusters annotated as Glia Mucosal/Type III recur across many datasets, suggesting a conserved mucosal glial state. We therefore treat this as a robust mucosal glial subtype with moderate-confidence mapping to the CL type 3 mucosal glia term. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes

labels.name: SMC Inner Muscle Cells
labels.rationale: SMC with FOXF2 and MORN5, likely inner circular smooth muscle layer of gut wall. Tissue section should be checked for these to ensure not myofibroblast

labels.name: Glia Extra-Ganglionic
labels.rationale: This label is used for enteric glia captured outside of well-formed myenteric and submucosal ganglia, especially in biopsy-derived datasets. Clusters annotated as Glia Extra-Ganglionic show a broad glial program (NRXN1, S100B, SOX10, PLP1) without clear plexus-restricted signatures and are the dominant glial population in mucosal samples.
labels.ontologyAssessment: need a term for glia on enteric neurons outside the ganglia (mucosa enervating neuron glia)

labels.name: Fibroblastic reticular cells
labels.rationale: Fibroblastic reticular cells are defined by expression of CCL19, CCL21, TNFSF13B and CXCL13 and cluster within lymphoid-enriched regions, consistent with FRCs organizing lymphoid tissue. Multiple clusters labeled as Fibroblastic reticular cells show similar marker profiles across datasets and samples, while a related cluster (Stroma_19_0) expresses RANKL and CXCL14 and may correspond to mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer cells. We note that FRC and mLTo-like states have some overlap. we annotate them with the intestinal fibroblastic reticular cell term and note the close relationship to mLTo.

labels.name: Pericytes Angiogenic
labels.rationale: HIGD1B expression marks pericytes engaged in vascular sprouting and angiogenesis

labels.name: SMC Outer Muscle Cells
labels.rationale: Outer longitudinal layer smooth muscle; distinguished from IMC by low FOXF2. Tissue section should be checked for these to ensure not myofibroblast

labels.name: Fibroblasts Subserosal
labels.rationale: Fibroblasts annotated as Subserosal are enriched for DPT, C7 and POSTN and tend to form deeper fibroblast clusters with lower dataset diversity (for example Stroma_8_0 and 8_1). We note that some clusters labeled as Subserosal in the original annotations appear in many biopsy-derived datasets, so we question whether they are truly subserosal versus generally deeper S3 fibroblasts. Do we need a deeper S3 fibroblast annotation? We therefore sometimes use the Intestinal Subserosal Fibroblasts and sometimes S3 term for DPT+/C7+/POSTN+ deeper fibroblasts while acknowledging that the exact boundary between subserosal and submucosal S3 fibroblasts is still being refined.

labels.name: vascular endothelial
labels.rationale: This grouping term is used for generic vascular endothelial cells expressing PECAM1, CDH5 and PLVAP that do not clearly fall into arteriolar, capillary, venular or lymphatic categories. Experts here noted that some clusters labeled vascular endothelial contain AQP1 and fibroblast genes and may represent mixed, transitional, or unclearly clustered states, and that there are doublet clusters involving endothelial cells and S2 fibroblasts. It's just one subcluster here that could be refined further with more evidence

labels.name: Pericytes Contractile
labels.rationale: Defined by RERGL and NTRK2, suggesting a pericyte subset with enhanced contractile apparatus.

labels.name: Glia Intra-Ganglionic
labels.rationale: This label corresponds to glia located within enteric ganglia, matching the type I enteric glial cell definition and showing enrichment for APOE, FRZB, RLBP1, CRYM and other neuro-supportive genes. Clusters annotated as Glia Intra-Ganglionic are present across multiple datasets and sit transcriptionally between myenteric and submucosal plexus glia, consistent with the canonical intra-ganglionic location.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Lymphatic
labels.rationale: Lymphatic endothelial cells are here defined by LYVE1, PROX1, MMRN1 and MRC1 and form multiple clusters (Stroma_13_1–13_5) that are present across many datasets, including immune-interacting states.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Capillary
labels.rationale: CD36, CLDN5, RAMP2, FLT1 and IGFBP7, consistent with gut micro capillary networks described in human intestinal single cell atlases.

labels.name: vascular endothelial Lacteals
labels.rationale: Lacteals here were annotated due to a strong fatty acid and glycerol uptake program. We should check if stroma_13_0 are present mostly in duodenum, consistent with villus lacteals being more prominent in small intestine. RELN here points to crypt

labels.name: Pericytes Immature
labels.rationale: We identified these with NDUFA4L2, PDGFRB and CSPG4 expression. Not sure about the latter two.

labels.name: Fibroblasts mLTo Cells (mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer cells)
labels.rationale: Clusters annotated as Fibroblasts mLTo Cells show expression of RANKL (TNFSF11), CXCL14 and other lymphoid-organizing genes in addition to a fibroblast matrix program, and Stroma_19_0 especially "could be mLTo because RANKL, CXCL14, TNFSF11". These cells likely represent a specialized organizer subset related to fibroblastic reticular cells but with stronger RANKL-driven lymphoid organizing functions. The population is relatively small and has moderate dataset diversity, consistent with tissue-restricted lymphoid niches, so we annotate it as a candidate mesenchymal lymphoid tissue organizer fibroblast class.

labels.name: Fibroblasts Myofibroblasts
labels.rationale: Myofibroblasts and SMCs could be mixed up in some places. I had used HHIF to annotated SMCs but in absense of GREM1/GREM2 it's possible these SMCs are really myofibroblasts.

labels.name: Glia Muscularis propria/Type IV
labels.rationale: This label captures glia associated with the muscularis propria that show markers such as SLC5A7, APOD and KCNS3 in addition to a core glial program. These clusters are enriched in full-thickness specimens with abundant muscle, and rare or absent in superficial biopsies, consistent with a muscularis propria localization. The glial subtypes performed poorly in reference mapping benchmarks, so a lesser resolution is likely best for the data currently. Annotation experts also point to less confidence in glial subtypes
